open_points.subject: Python runtime digest
open_points.question: What concrete Python runtime artifact must the required digest identify and compare: a distribution archive, an executable, the complete installed runtime tree, or a containing image constituent?
options: Digest the exact Python distribution archive used to install the runtime.
Digest the complete installed Python runtime tree.
Treat the base-image digest as fixing Python and require no separate Python artifact digest.
open_points.default_guess: Digest the exact Python distribution artifact from which the runtime is installed.

witness.initial: A release names Python 3.13.1 and records a digest; its interpreter executable is unchanged, but one standard-library file in the installed runtime tree has been replaced.
events: The release process builds the release and records the digest of the Python executable.
The installer compares the executable and then examines the installed runtime.
The installer attempts to start the release.
outcomes: The digest matches the executable, so installation succeeds and the instance starts.
The digest is defined over the runtime tree, so it differs; installation fails and no instance starts.

set_aside.subject: dependency digest policy
set_aside.question: Which digest algorithm or allowed algorithm set provides the required verification, and is an unrecognized or weaker digest refused?
options: Require one fixed collision-resistant algorithm, such as SHA-256.
Permit a closed, versioned set of collision-resistant algorithms and require the algorithm identifier with each digest.
Accept whatever digest form the release tooling supports.
set_aside.default_guess: Require SHA-256 for every dependency digest and refuse every other or malformed digest.

witness.initial: A release lists the expected bytes of a Python package with an exact version and a digest value, but no digest algorithm is identified.
events: The release producer computes the listed value with SHA-256.
The installer interprets an unqualified digest as SHA-512, or accepts only SHA-512.
outcomes: The installer verifies the SHA-256 value and starts the instance.
The installer cannot verify the value and fails the installation, so no instance starts.
witness.observer: The owner deploying the same release

set_aside.subject: release identity
set_aside.text: the same release installed again gives the same list
set_aside.question: What makes two installations the same release, and may a release identifier or tag ever be rebound to different release contents?
options: A release is identified by an immutable digest of its complete release manifest; labels may move but do not define identity.
A version string identifies a release and is permanently immutable once published.
A version string or tag may be rebound, and rebinding constitutes a new release.
set_aside.default_guess: Identify a release by an immutable digest of its complete manifest and reject publication that reuses a version for different contents.

witness.initial: Release label 1.4 initially denotes manifest A, whose dependency list contains package P 2.0; an instance of it has been installed.
events: The publisher changes label 1.4 to manifest B, whose dependency list contains P 2.1.
outcomes: The label denotes the same release, so rebinding is refused or the second installation must still use manifest A and P 2.0.
Manifest B is treated as a new release despite reusing the label, so the installation uses P 2.1.
witness.observer: The owner comparing the two installations

set_aside.subject: runtime loading from outside the release
set_aside.text: Registry has no dependency that loads code at run time from outside its release.
set_aside.question: When a release contains a reachable facility that would load code from outside the release, which required outcome applies: must the release not be made, must installation fail, or may the release run provided every such load attempt is refused?
options: The release is not made if any admissible runtime path can load external code.
Installation fails when such a facility or configuration is detected, and no instance starts.
The release may be installed, but every attempted external code load is refused before any external bytes execute.
set_aside.default_guess: Do not make a release containing any admissible runtime path that can load code from outside it.

witness.initial: Registry code contains an enabled plugin path that fetches and imports a module from a configured HTTPS URL; the dependency list contains no such module.
events: The release process evaluates the candidate release.
The owner attempts to install it.
After start, a request reaches the plugin path.
outcomes: The candidate is not made as a release, so it cannot be installed.
The release is made and installed, but the runtime refuses the plugin request before fetching or executing code.
witness.observer: The owner, who sees whether the release can be installed and run
